outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Foundations of Tabular Learning and the LLM Revolution
outline.description: This chapter introduces the challenges of few-shot learning in tabular data, reviews the evolution of Large Language Models (LLMs) in this domain, and identifies the critical limitations of current end-to-end LLM approaches that motivate the need for a new paradigm.
subtopics: The unique challenges of tabular data: heterogeneity and low-shot regimes
Overview of traditional few-shot learning techniques (pre-training, augmentation, transfer learning)
The rise of LLMs in reasoning and their application to structured data
Limitations of current LLM-based tabular methods: inference cost, fine-tuning requirements, and prompt size constraints
Defining the problem: Why we need a feature engineering approach rather than direct prediction

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: The FeatLLM Framework: Conceptual Overview
outline.description: This chapter provides a high-level introduction to the FeatLLM framework, explaining its core philosophy of treating LLMs as 'feature engineers' rather than 'predictors.' It outlines the end-to-end workflow from rule generation to final prediction.
subtopics: Core philosophy: Shifting from end-to-end prediction to automated feature engineering
The two-stage process: Rule extraction and likelihood inference
The role of simple downstream models (linear regression) vs. complex LLM inference
Key advantages: API-only access, elimination of per-sample LLM queries, and robustness to large feature sets
Visualizing the FeatLLM pipeline

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Prompt Engineering for Rule Extraction
outline.description: This chapter details the specific prompt design strategies used to guide LLMs in extracting high-quality decision rules. It covers how to structure prompts to leverage prior knowledge and avoid spurious correlations.
subtopics: Component 1: Basic information description (task formulation, feature definitions, serialization)
Component 2: Reasoning instructions (Chain-of-Thought integration)
Step-by-step reasoning: Inferring causal relationships before deducing specific rules
Component 3: Response instructions (formatting rules for programmatic parsing)
Strategies for handling categorical vs. numerical features in rule generation
Preventing overfitting and underfitting through fixed rule counts

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 4: From Natural Language Rules to Binary Features
outline.description: This chapter explains the technical implementation of converting LLM-generated natural language rules into executable code. It addresses the challenges of parsing noisy text output and creating binary feature vectors.
subtopics: The challenge of parsing noisy natural language outputs from LLMs
Meta-prompting: Using an LLM to generate Python code from natural language rules
Executing generated code safely using Python's `exec()` function
Constructing binary feature vectors ($z_k^i$) based on rule satisfaction
Handling syntactic variations (e.g., 'greater than' vs. '>') via semantic understanding
